title: slice
body:
## slice

Cuts the input with one infinite plane through origin, perpendicular to normal, and returns polygonal data: a surface from a volume mesh, lines from a surface. Point arrays are interpolated onto the cut and cell arrays are copied from the cell each polygon came from, so cell-centred CFD fields appear piecewise constant. Use it for cross-sections of 3-D fields; use clip to keep one side of a volume, contour for an isosurface, probeLine for a 1-D profile, and pvSlice for several parallel offsets or other cut shapes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- origin defaults to [0, 0, 0], not to the centre of your data as in the ParaView GUI. A plane that misses the data gives empty geometry, which Schemaxis reports as EMPTY_GEOMETRY; set origin inside the dataset bounds.
- Hyper tree grid input is refused with INPUT_TRAIT_MISMATCH (recovery: use pvSlice): this operation sets only ParaView's SliceType, whereas a hyper tree grid is cut by the separate HyperTreeGridImplicitFunction, so origin and normal would have no effect on it.
- Native acceptance (examples/schemaxis/acceptance.py) checks that slices lie on the requested plane and that integrals over a wavelet slice match analytic values; crinkle output and real CFD meshes are not separately checked.

Native constructor: `Slice`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). A hyper-tree grid is refused with INPUT_TRAIT_MISMATCH when the node updates; use pvSlice for it. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{"topology":["structured","unstructured"]},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"},"recovery":"use pvSlice, which exposes the native hyper-tree-grid cut function"}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origin` | A point lying on the cutting plane, expressed as [X, Y, Z] in dataset coordinates. Moving it along the normal moves the cut. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane. Use z+ for an XY plane, y+ for XZ, and x+ for YZ; a nonzero XYZ vector or declared direction object also works. | `{"type":"union","title":"direction","summary":"An axis token, a vector, or an azimuth and elevation about an up axis","options":[{"type":"string","title":"axis token such as 'x+' or 'z-'"},{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3},{"type":"object","title":"direction object","properties":{"axis":{"type":"string","summary":"Axis token such as 'x+'"},"azimuth":{"type":"number","minimum":-360,"maximum":360,"summary":"Degrees about the up axis from the reference axis"},"elevation":{"type":"number","minimum":-180,"maximum":180,"summary":"Degrees tilted from the plane perpendicular to up"},"vector":{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3},"up":{"type":"union","title":"up direction","options":[{"type":"string","title":"axis token such as 'z+'"},{"type":"array","title":"vector [x, y, z]","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}]}}}]}` | `[1,0,0]` | `[1,0,0]` |
| `crinkle` | Keep whole intersected cells instead of interpolating a flat geometric cut. This is useful for inspecting mesh cells but changes the output geometry. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` | `false` |
| `triangulate` | Split the interpolated cut polygons into triangles. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "slice",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  }
}
```
